habitat: Subtropical/tropical moist montane forests; rocky streams and gullies in mountains
story: The Bornean Whistling Thrush (Myophonus borneensis) is an extraordinary bird that belongs to the Muscicapidae family. It is most commonly observed in Subtropical/tropical moist montane forests; rocky streams and gullies in mountains, where its behaviors contribute to the ecological dynamics of the area. Listed as Least Concern (LC) by the IUCN, this species' future depends on continued conservation action. The story of the Bornean Whistling Thrush is one of adaptation and resilience, offering valuable lessons for conservationists. This poster aims to bring the Bornean Whistling Thrush into focus, highlighting its beauty and the importance of its habitat.
